bibliographic_hint: Suetonius. "Divus Augustus" (Life of Augustus), in De Vita Caesarum (The Twelve Caesars). Written c. 120 CE.
notes: Closest contemporary biography; includes personal details, appearance, character, death scene

bibliographic_hint: Cassius Dio. Roman History, Books 45–56. Written c. 200–230 CE.
notes: Most detailed continuous narrative of Augustus career; primary source for constitutional settlements of 27 BCE and 23 BCE

bibliographic_hint: Appian. Bella Civilia (Civil Wars), Books 3–5. Written mid-2nd century CE.
notes: Key source for Second Triumvirate period, proscriptions, war against Sextus Pompeius

bibliographic_hint: Res Gestae Divi Augusti. Composed by Augustus before his death. Most complete copy: Monumentum Ancyranum, Ankara, Turkey.
notes: First-person funerary inscription by Augustus; self-presentation, NOT neutral history; omits defeats and selectively narrates achievements

bibliographic_hint: Tacitus. Annales (Annals), Book 1. Written c. 115–120 CE.
notes: Retrospective assessment of Augustus death and legacy; skeptical toward the Principate

bibliographic_hint: Plutarch. "Life of Antony" (Antonius), in Bioi Paralleloi (Parallel Lives). Written c. 100–120 CE.
notes: Covers the rivalry between Octavian and Mark Antony

bibliographic_hint: Nicolaus of Damascus. Life of Augustus. Written late 1st century BCE.
notes: Contemporary account by a court historian of Herod; valuable for Octavian early life

bibliographic_hint: Velleius Paterculus. Roman History. Written c. 30 CE.
notes: Serving officer under Tiberius; strongly pro-Augustan perspective

bibliographic_hint: Cicero. Philippics; Epistulae ad Atticum (Letters to Atticus). 44–43 BCE.
notes: Contemporary source; initially allied with Octavian against Antony; uses name Octavianus

bibliographic_hint: Syme, Ronald. The Roman Revolution. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1939.
notes: Foundational modern work; portrays Augustus as revolutionary who cloaked autocracy in republican language

bibliographic_hint: Goldsworthy, Adrian. Augustus: First Emperor of Rome. New Haven: Yale University Press, 2014.
notes: Modern biography emphasizing that the Principate developed through trial and experimentation

bibliographic_hint: Wikipedia contributors. "Augustus." Wikipedia, The Free Encyclopedia.
notes: Comprehensive overview with citations to both ancient and modern sources; used as clue only

bibliographic_hint: Vatican Museums. Augustus of Prima Porta, Braccio Nuovo, inventory no. 2290.
notes: Primary museum holding record for the most famous Augustus portrait statue

bibliographic_hint: Museo Nazionale Romano, Palazzo Massimo. Via Labicana Augustus (Augustus as Pontifex Maximus).
Eck, Werner. The Age of Augustus. 2nd ed. Oxford: Blackwell, 2007.
notes: Concise scholarly overview of Augustan period

bibliographic_hint: Southern, Pat. Augustus. 2nd ed. London: Routledge, 2014.
Wiseman, T.P. "The House of Augustus and the Lupercal." Journal of Roman Archaeology (2025).
notes: Argues that Augustus positive contemporary reception should be taken seriously

bibliographic_hint: Augustan coinage with imperial portrait (denarii, aurei). Various numismatic collections.
notes: Coins proclaim CAESAR AVGVSTVS, DIVI F, PATER PATRIAE; contemporary official imagery
